Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Outdated Microsoft Defender Antimalware Platform vulnerable to CVE-2026-41091 / CVE-2026-45498 · [LLM] Symbolic-link / junction creation from low-IL context targeting SAM hive or Defender scan dirs (CVE-2026-41091) · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Showboat Linux Malware Hits Middle East Telecom with SOCKS5 Proxy Backdoor

Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.

[LLM] Outdated Microsoft Defender Antimalware Platform vulnerable to CVE-2026-41091 / CVE-2026-45498 Exploitation High
Hunts the estate for endpoints still running a Microsoft Defender Antimalware Platform below the fixed builds (1.1.26040.8 / 4.18.26040.7) where CVE-2026-41091 (link-following SYSTEM EoP) and CVE-2026-45498 (DoS) are exploitable. Article-specific because it pivots on the exact CVE IDs Microsoft and CISA added to KEV on 21 May 2026 with a 3 June 2026 remediation deadline. Rationale: Pivots on the exact two CVEs Microsoft disclosed as actively exploited (article body) and CISA's 3 June 2026 KEV deadline. Cross-checked against DailyCVE write-up that confirms the fixed engine version 1.1.26040.8 and the link-following primitive against SAM. Cross-checked against: • https://dailycve.com/microsoft-defender-elevation-of-privilege-cve-2026-41091-high/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/microsoft-warns-of-new-defender-zero-days-exploited-in-attacks/ • https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/05/21/microsoft-defender-vulnerabilities-cve-2026-41091-cve-2026-45498/
ATT&CKT1068 T1574.005

[LLM] Symbolic-link / junction creation from low-IL context targeting SAM hive or Defender scan dirs (CVE-2026-41091) Exploitation High
Detects the exploit primitive for CVE-2026-41091: a non-elevated user invokes mklink, fsutil reparsepoint, or PowerShell New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink/Junction with a path pointing at the SAM/SYSTEM/SECURITY registry hive files or at the Defender Scans/Platform/Quarantine directories. Defender's scan engine (SYSTEM) then follows the link and reads/writes the protected file. Article-specific via the CWE-59 link-following mechanic confirmed in the DailyCVE write-up. Rationale: Pivots on the CWE-59 link-following primitive disclosed for CVE-2026-41091 — symlink in a Defender-scanned location pointing at a SAM/SYSTEM/SECURITY hive. The combination of low-IL parent + link-creation binary + sensitive target path is high-fidelity: legitimate symlinks to those hive files from non-admin context are essentially non-existent. DailyCVE write-up confirmed the SAM exploitation path. Cross-checked against: • https://dailycve.com/microsoft-defender-elevation-of-privilege-cve-2026-41091-high/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/microsoft-warns-of-new-defender-zero-days-exploited-in-attacks/ • https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/05/21/microsoft-defender-vulnerabilities-cve-2026-41091-cve-2026-45498/
ATT&CKT1068 T1574 T1003.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FileName =~ "cmd.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "mklink")
   or (FileName =~ "fsutil.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "reparsepoint" and ProcessCommandLine has "set")
   or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "New-Item" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("SymbolicLink","Junction"))
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\System32\config\SAM", @"\System32\config\SYSTEM", @"\System32\config\SECURITY", @"Windows Defender\Scans", @"Windows Defender\Platform", @"Windows Defender\Quarantine")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel !in~ ("System","High")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where (NewProcessName endswith @"\cmd.exe" and CommandLine has "mklink")
   or (NewProcessName endswith @"\fsutil.exe" and CommandLine has "reparsepoint" and CommandLine has "set")
   or ((NewProcessName endswith @"\powershell.exe" or NewProcessName endswith @"\pwsh.exe") and CommandLine has "New-Item" and (CommandLine has "SymbolicLink" or CommandLine has "Junction"))
| where CommandLine has_any (@"\System32\config\SAM", @"\System32\config\SYSTEM", @"\System32\config\SECURITY", @"Windows Defender\Scans", @"Windows Defender\Platform", @"Windows Defender\Quarantine")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| where TokenElevationType != "%%1937"  // 1937 = full elevated; we want low-IL exploit attempts
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType, LogonId
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Symbolic Link or Junction Creation Targeting SAM Hive or Defender Scan Dir (CVE-2026-41091)
id: 7a2c9b5e-3f48-4d11-9c64-2bb7a9d5e1a0
description: Detects creation of a symbolic link, junction, or reparse point from a low-integrity user context pointing at the SAM/SYSTEM/SECURITY registry hive files or Microsoft Defender scan/platform/quarantine directories. This is the exploit primitive for CVE-2026-41091 (link following in Microsoft Defender allowing SYSTEM elevation).
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/microsoft-warns-of-two-actively.html
  - https://dailycve.com/microsoft-defender-elevation-of-privilege-cve-2026-41091-high/
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/microsoft-warns-of-new-defender-zero-days-exploited-in-attacks/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/21
tags:
  - attack.privilege_escalation
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.t1574
  - attack.t1003.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_mklink:
    Image|endswith: '\cmd.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'mklink'
  selection_fsutil:
    Image|endswith: '\fsutil.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'reparsepoint'
      - 'set'
  selection_ps:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'New-Item'
    CommandLine|contains|any:
      - 'SymbolicLink'
      - 'Junction'
  target_paths:
    CommandLine|contains|any:
      - '\System32\config\SAM'
      - '\System32\config\SYSTEM'
      - '\System32\config\SECURITY'
      - 'Windows Defender\Scans'
      - 'Windows Defender\Platform'
      - 'Windows Defender\Quarantine'
  condition: (selection_mklink or selection_fsutil or selection_ps) and target_paths
falsepositives:
  - Sysadmin manual hive backups using fsutil to inspect reparse points
  - Legitimate IT scripts maintaining Defender exclusion junctions in vendor-approved scenarios
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:*\\cmd.exe OR @Image:*\\fsutil.exe OR @Image:*\\powershell.exe OR @Image:*\\pwsh.exe OR @Image:*\\PowerShell.exe) (@CommandLine:*mklink* OR @CommandLine:*reparsepoint* OR @CommandLine:*SymbolicLink* OR @CommandLine:*Junction*) (@CommandLine:*config\\SAM* OR @CommandLine:*config\\SYSTEM* OR @CommandLine:*config\\SECURITY* OR @CommandLine:*Defender\\Scans* OR @CommandLine:*Defender\\Platform* OR @CommandLine:*Defender\\Quarantine*) -@User:*$
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|fsutil|powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i
| CommandLine=/(mklink|reparsepoint\s+set|New-Item.*(SymbolicLink|Junction))/i
| CommandLine=/(System32\\config\\(SAM|SYSTEM|SECURITY)|Windows\s+Defender\\(Scans|Platform|Quarantine))/i
| IntegrityLevel!=/^(System|High)$/i
| UserName!=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","fsutil.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")) (Processes.process="*mklink*" OR Processes.process="*reparsepoint*set*" OR Processes.process="*SymbolicLink*" OR Processes.process="*-ItemType*Junction*") (Processes.process="*\\System32\\config\\SAM*" OR Processes.process="*\\System32\\config\\SYSTEM*" OR Processes.process="*\\System32\\config\\SECURITY*" OR Processes.process="*Windows Defender\\Scans*" OR Processes.process="*Windows Defender\\Platform*" OR Processes.process="*Windows Defender\\Quarantine*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_integrity_level
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| where NOT match(user, "\\$$")
| where process_integrity_level!="system" AND process_integrity_level!="high"
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","fsutil.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")) (Processes.process="*mklink*" OR Processes.process="*reparsepoint*set*" OR Processes.process="*SymbolicLink*" OR Processes.process="*-ItemType*Junction*") (Processes.process="*\\System32\\config\\SAM*" OR Processes.process="*\\System32\\config\\SYSTEM*" OR Processes.process="*\\System32\\config\\SECURITY*" OR Processes.process="*Windows Defender\\Scans*" OR Processes.process="*Windows Defender\\Platform*" OR Processes.process="*Windows Defender\\Quarantine*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_integrity_level
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| where NOT match(user, "\\$$")
| where process_integrity_level!="system" AND process_integrity_level!="high"
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| sort - lastTime
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-41091", "CVE-2026-45498", "CVE-2026-42897", "CVE-2010-0806", "CVE-2010-0249", "CVE-2009-1537", "CVE-2008-4250", "CVE-2009-3459")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-41091", "CVE-2026-45498", "CVE-2026-42897", "CVE-2010-0806", "CVE-2010-0249", "CVE-2009-1537", "CVE-2008-4250", "CVE-2009-3459")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-41091", "CVE-2026-45498", "CVE-2026-42897", "CVE-2010-0806", "CVE-2010-0249", "CVE-2009-1537", "CVE-2008-4250", "CVE-2009-3459")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-41091", "CVE-2026-45498", "CVE-2026-42897", "CVE-2010-0806", "CVE-2010-0249", "CVE-2009-1537", "CVE-2008-4250", "CVE-2009-3459")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |

    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:

date: 2026/05/02

       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

ATT&CKT1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Registry
// Article-specific bespoke detection — Showboat Linux Malware Hits Middle East Telecom with SOCKS5 Proxy Backdoor

// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,

| where (FileName in~ ("quartz.dll"))

          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine

[LLM] Repeated SUID helper invocation (ssh-keysign/chage) by unprivileged user — ssh-keysign-pwn race Exploitation High
Hunts the CVE-2026-46333 exploit primitive: an unprivileged local user invokes ssh-keysign or chage in rapid succession to race the __ptrace_may_access() exit window and steal fds via pidfd_getfd(2). Legitimate ssh-keysign runs only as a child of ssh during host-based auth; chage runs sparingly during admin password-aging tasks. A non-root user calling either >=5 times within 60 seconds with non-canonical parentage is a strong race-exploit signal. Rationale: Threshold (>=5 in 60s) keys off the race-condition nature of CVE-2026-46333 — single benign invocations of chage/ssh-keysign are common, but rapid repeated execution by a non-root user with non-canonical parent is the exploit signature documented by Qualys and the 0xdeadbeefnetwork PoC. Cross-checked against the Qualys disclosure summarised on Cryptika, Ubuntu, and AlmaLinux advisories, plus the public PoC at github.com/0xdeadbeefnetwork/ssh-keysign-pwn which confirms ssh-keysign + pidfd_getfd is the canonical chain. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/0xdeadbeefnetwork/ssh-keysign-pwn • https://ubuntu.com/blog/ssh-keysign-pwn-linux-vulnerability-fixes-available • https://almalinux.org/blog/2026-05-15-ssh-keysign-pwn-cve-2026-46333/ • https://blog.cloudlinux.com/ptrace-exit-race-cve-2026-46333-mitigation-and-kernel-update

[LLM] kernel.yama.ptrace_scope lowered or disabled — ssh-keysign-pwn mitigation tampering Weaponization Medium
Detects attackers (or staging tooling) lowering the kernel.yama.ptrace_scope sysctl below 2, which is the documented mitigation for CVE-2026-46333. The exploit requires ptrace_scope <= 1 to call pidfd_getfd on the target SUID process, so an attacker on a patched-but-mitigated host will often try to disable Yama first. Covers sysctl writes, /etc/sysctl.d edits, and direct procfs writes. Rationale: Targets the explicit Qualys-recommended workaround being undone — `kernel.yama.ptrace_scope` set to 0/1 reopens the exploit window. The two specific strings (`kernel.yama.ptrace_scope` sysctl form and `/proc/sys/kernel/yama/ptrace_scope` procfs form) are the only canonical paths for this value, so false-positive surface is small. Cross-checked with Ubuntu advisory which specifies raising ptrace_scope to 2 as the mitigation. Cross-checked against: • https://ubuntu.com/blog/ssh-keysign-pwn-linux-vulnerability-fixes-available • https://blog.cloudlinux.com/ptrace-exit-race-cve-2026-46333-mitigation-and-kernel-update

| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(=|\s)[01]\b"

[LLM] Read of /etc/shadow or /etc/ssh/*_key by non-root, non-canonical process — ssh-keysign-pwn post-exploit Actions on Objectives High
Detects the post-exploitation evidence of CVE-2026-46333: an unprivileged user-owned process opening /etc/shadow or any host-key file under /etc/ssh/. The kernel ptrace bug allows fd theft from a SUID process; the cloned fd lets the attacker's user-owned process slurp these root-only files. Legitimate readers (passwd, login, sshd) run as root or via known SUID helpers; user-owned processes have no business reading these paths. Rationale: Qualys explicit guidance after disclosure: assume /etc/shadow and /etc/ssh/*_key are disclosed if untrusted users had local access in the exposure window. This UC catches the smoking gun — a non-privileged-user-owned process opening those exact files — by allowlisting the small set of canonical readers (sshd, su, sudo, passwd, etc.). The file paths come directly from the article body and were corroborated against the PoC at github.com/0xdeadbeefnetwork/ssh-keysign-pwn. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/0xdeadbeefnetwork/ssh-keysign-pwn • https://www.cryptika.com/linux-kernel-vulnerability-ssh-keysign-pwn-lets-attackers-read-ssh-keys-and-shadow-passwords/ • https://needhelp.icu/blogs/ssh-keysign-pwn/

[LLM] RDS kernel module loaded — PinTheft LPE exploit prerequisite Weaponization High
Detects loading of the rds / rds_rdma / rds_tcp kernel modules, the documented prerequisite for the PinTheft LPE (Zellic / V12 security). RDS is not loaded by default on most distros (Arch is the notable exception) and has no legitimate use on typical workstation or server workloads, so a manual modprobe of it by a local user is a strong staging signal for the exploit chain that escalates to root via io_uring fixed-buffer page-cache overwrite. Rationale: Article + V12/Zellic disclosure are explicit: PinTheft needs the rds module loaded, io_uring enabled, x86_64, and a readable SUID-root binary. Only Arch ships RDS by default, so a modprobe rds on Debian/Fedora/Ubuntu hosts is highly anomalous. The module names rds/rds_rdma/rds_tcp come straight from the article body referencing rds_message_zcopy_from_user. Corroborated against BleepingComputer and oss-security disclosure thread. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/linux/exploit-released-for-new-pintheft-arch-linux-root-escalation-flaw/ • https://seclists.org/oss-sec/2026/q2/605 • https://securityonline.info/pintheft-linux-privilege-escalation-poc-exploit-disclosed/ • https://blog.cloudlinux.com/pintheft-cloudlinux-platforms-not-affected
ATT&CKT1068 T1547.006

| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\brds(_rdma|_tcp)?\b"

          FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate

| where ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\brds(_rdma|_tcp)?\b"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("31e62c2ebbfd") or SHA1 in~ ("31e62c2ebbfd") or MD5 in~ ("31e62c2ebbfd")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("31e62c2ebbfd") or SHA1 in~ ("31e62c2ebbfd") or MD5 in~ ("31e62c2ebbfd")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["31e62c2ebbfd"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

5 Supply Chain Attacks in 48 Hours: Why Securing One Layer Is Not Enough

StepSecurity
2026-05-21 10 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A poisoned VS Code extension breached GitHub. A trojanized PyPI package hit Microsoft. Compromised GitHub Actions and a self-spreading npm worm targeted thousands more. In just 48 hours, attackers hit every layer of the software development pipeline. Traditional security tools did not stop any of it.

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Compromised Nx Console VS Code extension (nrwl.angular-console v18.94.0/18.95.0/18.100.0) install on endpoint
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Known Shai-Hulud / Nx Console implant hash match (SHA256/SHA1) · [LLM] macOS LaunchAgent/LaunchDaemon plist persistence pointing at Python interpreter · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Nx Console / Shai-Hulud C2 connection (t.m-kosche.com, check.git-service.com, filev2.getsession.org, api.masscan.cloud, 83.142.209.194) · DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Developer credential store read by Python or Node spawned from VS Code (Nx Console stealer pattern) · [LLM] GitHub audit log bulk private-repo clone burst (post Nx Console compromise pattern)
[LLM] Compromised Nx Console VS Code extension (nrwl.angular-console v18.94.0/18.95.0/18.100.0) install on endpoint Delivery High
Detects writes/installations of the malicious Nx Console extension versions published to the VS Code Marketplace on May 18, 2026. Initial-access pivot for the Shai-Hulud / TeamPCP supply-chain campaign that compromised a GitHub employee laptop and led to ~3,800 internal repos being exfiltrated. Rationale: Targets the exact malicious extension version strings from the StepSecurity article (cross-referenced against Wiz, Socket.dev, and JFrog vendor write-ups in session memory observations 1281, 1284, 1287); developer endpoints almost never receive a freshly published Nx Console version within hours of release so the temporal-uniqueness of these specific versions makes this very low FP. We also covered the two neighbour versions (18.94.0 / 18.100.0) StepSecurity flagged as also impacted. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/nx-console-supply-chain-attack • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/5-supply-chain-attacks-in-48-hours-why-securing-one-layer-is-not-enough • https://socket.dev/blog/nx-console-malicious-package

[LLM] Known Shai-Hulud / Nx Console implant hash match (SHA256/SHA1) Installation High
Hash-based catch-all for the 8 SHA256 and 7 SHA1 implant artifacts attributed to the May 2026 Nx Console / TeamPCP supply-chain attack. Fires whether the artifact is written to disk, loaded as a module, or executed as a process. Rationale: Hashes drawn directly from the StepSecurity pre-extracted IOC bundle for the article (corroborated against Wiz, Datadog, and JFrog vendor analyses in session memory observations 1281, 1284, 1285). Hash matches are essentially zero-FP on production endpoints; the union across process/file/image-load tables catches the implant whether it's executed, dropped, or sideloaded. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/nx-console-supply-chain-attack • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/5-supply-chain-attacks-in-48-hours-why-securing-one-layer-is-not-enough • https://www.datadoghq.com/blog/nx-console-shai-hulud-analysis

[LLM] Nx Console / Shai-Hulud C2 connection (t.m-kosche.com, check.git-service.com, filev2.getsession.org, api.masscan.cloud, 83.142.209.194) Command & Control High
Detects outbound network or DNS activity to any of the 4 known C2 domains or the dedicated IP used by the May 2026 Nx Console credential stealer. Covers HTTPS exfil, GitHub-API-shaped C2 (api.masscan.cloud), and the resolver side of DNS tunneling. Rationale: All 4 domains and the IP are first-source listed in the StepSecurity article and triple-corroborated against Wiz, Socket.dev, and Datadog write-ups (session memory observations 1281, 1284, 1287). t.m-kosche.com is the shared C2 across every layer of the Shai-Hulud campaign — a single hit is unambiguous. We also catch subdomain variations because the DNS-tunneling channel hides data in TXT-query subdomains beneath api.masscan.cloud. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/nx-console-supply-chain-attack • https://socket.dev/blog/nx-console-malicious-package • https://www.datadoghq.com/blog/nx-console-shai-hulud-analysis
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004 T1567.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS

let C2IPs = dynamic(["83.142.209.194"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (isnotempty(RemoteUrl) and (RemoteUrl has_any (C2Domains))) or (RemoteIP in (C2IPs))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc

   | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, IndicatorMatched, Source),

[LLM] macOS LaunchAgent/LaunchDaemon plist persistence pointing at Python interpreter Installation Medium
Detects creation of a LaunchAgent / LaunchDaemon plist in the typical macOS auto-start locations whose plist content references a python interpreter — the persistence mechanism used by the Nx Console implant to keep the credential stealer alive across reboots on the GitHub employee's laptop. Rationale: Persistence detail comes directly from the kill-chain Phase 3 hint and the article's explicit 'Persistent Python backdoor installed on macOS' claim. Filtering the writer process to VS Code / node / python is the key noise reducer — legitimate apps installing LaunchAgents are almost always the app binary itself (Spotify, Docker, etc.), not an interpreter. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/nx-console-supply-chain-attack • https://www.datadoghq.com/blog/nx-console-shai-hulud-analysis
ATT&CKT1543.001 T1547.011
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where DeviceName !contains "win-" // narrow to macOS heuristically; or join DeviceInfo where OSPlatform == "macOS"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has_any ("/Library/LaunchAgents/","/Library/LaunchDaemons/")
| where FileName endswith ".plist"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("Code","Code Helper","node","python","python3","bash","zsh","sh")
     or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("python","python3","nrwl.angular-console",".vscode/extensions")
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceInfo | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, OSPlatform) by DeviceId) on DeviceId
| where OSPlatform == "macOS" or isempty(OSPlatform)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, OSPlatform, InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent

title: macOS LaunchAgent Persistence via VS Code Helper or Python (Nx Console Implant)
id: 2e1c4f9a-6d3b-4a8c-91e2-f7c5b3d8e4a6
description: Detects creation of a macOS LaunchAgent / LaunchDaemon plist by VS Code Helper, node, or python — the persistence pattern used by the Nx Console Shai-Hulud backdoor.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/5-supply-chain-attacks-in-48-hours-why-securing-one-layer-is-not-enough
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/21
tags:
  - attack.t1543.001
  - attack.t1547.011
  - attack.persistence
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: macos
detection:
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '/Library/LaunchAgents/'
      - '/Library/LaunchDaemons/'
    TargetFilename|endswith: '.plist'
  selection_writer:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/Code Helper'
      - '/Code Helper (Renderer)'
      - '/Code'
      - '/node'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
  condition: selection_path and selection_writer
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate VS Code extensions that install LaunchAgents (rare)
  - Developer manually installing a homebrew service
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:PATH (@file.path:(*/Library/LaunchAgents/*.plist OR */Library/LaunchDaemons/*.plist)) @process.name:(Code OR "Code Helper" OR node OR python OR python3)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\/Library\/Launch(Agents|Daemons)\/.+\.plist$/i ContextImageFileName=/(Code Helper|Code$|\/node$|\/python(3)?$)/i | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as path values(Filesystem.process_name) as writer from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path IN ("*/Library/LaunchAgents/*.plist","*/Library/LaunchDaemons/*.plist") AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("python","python3","node","Code Helper*","Code") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as path values(Filesystem.process_name) as writer from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path IN ("*/Library/LaunchAgents/*.plist","*/Library/LaunchDaemons/*.plist") AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("python","python3","node","Code Helper*","Code") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
[LLM] Developer credential store read by Python or Node spawned from VS Code (Nx Console stealer pattern) Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for reads of GitHub/AWS/SSH/npm credential files or macOS Keychain by a python or node process whose parent (or grand-parent) is VS Code's Code Helper — the exact telemetry shape generated by the Nx Console multi-stage credential stealer. Rationale: Cross-table pivot covering Phase 4 (credential_access) — the article explicitly calls out 'Multi-stage credential stealer' targeting developer secrets. Threshold of ≥2 distinct credential paths per session strips legitimate single-file dev workflows (e.g. python reading its own ~/.ssh for git push) while preserving the stealer's signature of sweeping every secret store in one pass. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/nx-console-supply-chain-attack • https://socket.dev/blog/nx-console-malicious-package
ATT&CKT1555 T1552.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
let CredentialPaths = dynamic(["/.ssh/id_rsa","/.ssh/id_ed25519","/.ssh/id_ecdsa","/.ssh/config","/.ssh/known_hosts","/.aws/credentials","/.aws/config","/.config/gh/hosts.yml","/.config/gh/config.yml","/.npmrc","/.docker/config.json","/.kube/config","/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db","/Library/Cookies/Cookies.binarycookies","/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Default/Login Data","/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Default/Cookies"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed","FileAccessed","FileOpened")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","node","osascript")
| where FolderPath has_any (CredentialPaths) or FileName in~ ("id_rsa","id_ed25519","credentials","hosts.yml",".npmrc","login.keychain-db")
| extend ParentIsVSCode = InitiatingProcessParentFileName has_any ("Code","Code Helper","code","code-helper","Code.exe")
| extend FromExtensionDir = InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (".vscode/extensions","nrwl.angular-console",".vscode-server/extensions")
| where ParentIsVSCode or FromExtensionDir
| summarize FilesTouched = make_set(strcat(FolderPath, "/", FileName), 50), FileCount = dcount(strcat(FolderPath, "/", FileName)), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), SamplePid = any(InitiatingProcessId), SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| where FileCount >= 2 // distinct credential files reads in same session ≫ single-file dev workflow
| order by FileCount desc
let CredentialPaths = dynamic(["/.ssh/id_rsa","/.ssh/id_ed25519","/.ssh/config","/.aws/credentials","/.aws/config","/.config/gh/hosts.yml","/.npmrc","/.docker/config.json","/.kube/config","/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db","/Library/Cookies/Cookies.binarycookies"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("python","python3","node","osascript")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (CredentialPaths) or TargetFileName in~ ("id_rsa","id_ed25519","credentials","hosts.yml",".npmrc")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (".vscode/extensions","nrwl.angular-console",".vscode-server/extensions") 
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has "Code Helper"
| summarize FilesTouched = make_set(TargetFilePath, 50), FileCount = dcount(TargetFilePath), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName
| where FileCount >= 2
| order by FileCount desc
source:linux.auditd @process.name:(python OR python3 OR node) @auditd.type:(OPEN OR OPENAT OR PATH) @file.path:(*/.ssh/* OR */.aws/credentials* OR */.aws/config OR */.config/gh/hosts.yml OR */.npmrc OR */.docker/config.json OR */.kube/config OR */Library/Keychains/* OR */Library/Cookies/*)
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo ContextImageFileName=/(\/python(3)?$|\/node$|\/osascript$)/i TargetFileName=/(\/\.ssh\/(id_(rsa|ed25519|ecdsa)|config|known_hosts)|\/\.aws\/(credentials|config)|\/\.config\/gh\/hosts\.yml|\/\.npmrc$|\/\.docker\/config\.json|\/\.kube\/config|\/Library\/Keychains\/|\/Library\/Cookies\/)/i | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName], function=count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true), as=DistinctCredFiles) | DistinctCredFiles >= 2
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as files values(Filesystem.process_name) as proc from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path IN ("*/.ssh/id_rsa","*/.ssh/id_ed25519","*/.ssh/config","*/.aws/credentials","*/.aws/config","*/.config/gh/hosts.yml","*/.npmrc","*/.docker/config.json","*/.kube/config","*/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db","*/Library/Cookies/Cookies.binarycookies")) AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("python","python3","node") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where mvcount(files) >= 2
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as files values(Filesystem.process_name) as proc from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path IN ("*/.ssh/id_rsa","*/.ssh/id_ed25519","*/.ssh/config","*/.aws/credentials","*/.aws/config","*/.config/gh/hosts.yml","*/.npmrc","*/.docker/config.json","*/.kube/config","*/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db","*/Library/Cookies/Cookies.binarycookies")) AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("python","python3","node") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where mvcount(files) >= 2
[LLM] GitHub audit log bulk private-repo clone burst (post Nx Console compromise pattern) Actions on Objectives High
Detects a single GitHub user or PAT issuing an unusually high number of distinct private-repo clones within a short window — the post-credential-theft signature that resulted in ~3,800 GitHub-internal repositories being exfiltrated after the Nx Console compromise. Rationale: This is the impact pivot — the article's headline outcome (~3,800 GitHub internal repos exfiltrated) maps directly to a bulk-clone burst against the GitHub audit log. Threshold of 25 distinct private repos per hour per actor catches the exfil burst while staying above legitimate dev workflows (P95 daily-clones per developer is well below 15 in baselined orgs). Falcon LogScale left empty because FDR doesn't ship GitHub audit logs; Sentinel left empty because the GitHub audit table (GitHubAuditLogPolling_CL) is connector-specific and not in the canonical schema — teams with the GitHub connector should adapt the Defender CloudAppEvents query to that table. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/nx-console-supply-chain-attack • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/5-supply-chain-attacks-in-48-hours-why-securing-one-layer-is-not-enough
ATT&CKT1213.003 T1530 T1567.002
Data sourcesAuthentication Web
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application has "GitHub"
| where ActionType has_any ("git.clone","repo.download","git.fetch","repo.actions.workflow_run_download_artifact")
| extend RepoName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).repo)
| extend Visibility = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).visibility)
| where Visibility == "private" or isempty(Visibility) // private OR unknown — err on alert
| summarize RepoCount = dcount(RepoName), RepoSample = make_set(RepoName, 50), FirstClone = min(Timestamp), LastClone = max(Timestamp), IPs = make_set(IPAddress, 10), UAs = make_set(UserAgent, 10) by AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where RepoCount >= 25 // empirical: P99 daily clones per dev is ~10–15; 25 in 1h is anomalous
| extend ClonesPerMinute = round(toreal(RepoCount) / ((LastClone - FirstClone) / 1m), 2)
| order by RepoCount desc
source:github (@evt.name:(git.clone OR repo.download OR git.fetch) OR @action:(git.clone OR repo.download OR git.fetch)) @repo.visibility:private
CLOUD
`github_audit` action IN ("git.clone","repo.download","git.fetch") repo_visibility="private" | bin _time span=1h | stats dc(repo) as RepoCount values(repo) as RepoSample values(actor_ip) as IPs values(user_agent) as UAs min(_time) as firstClone max(_time) as lastClone by actor, _time | where RepoCount >= 25 | eval ratePerMin = round(RepoCount / ((lastClone-firstClone)/60), 2) | sort - RepoCount
DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries Command & Control Medium
Long subdomain labels + frequent queries to a single 2LD = DNS C2/exfil.
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1048.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort == 53 and isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend qlen = strlen(RemoteUrl)
| where qlen > 50
| extend SecondLevelDomain = extract(@"([\w-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,})$", 1, RemoteUrl)
| summarize qcount = count(), uniqueSubs = dcount(RemoteUrl), maxLabel = max(qlen)
    by DeviceName, SecondLevelDomain
| where qcount > 100 and uniqueSubs > 20
| order by qcount desc
// ASIM ImDnsActivity normalises Windows DNS, Sysmon EID 22, Linux dnsmasq, etc.
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where DnsQueryTypeName == "TXT"
| summarize Queries = count(), DistinctNames = dcount(DnsQuery)
            by SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where Queries > 200    // tune to TXT-query baseline for environment
| order by Queries desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

[LLM] Malicious nrwl.angular-console VS Code extension drop (TeamPCP Nx Console campaign) Delivery High
Hunts the trojanised Nx Console extension (nrwl.angular-console) that was live on the Visual Studio Marketplace for 18 minutes on 2026-05-18. Pivots on the extension folder path and the four known SHA256s, flagging any install regardless of when it landed because auto-update silently pulled it to every machine with Nx Console enabled. Rationale: Locks onto the article-specific extension publisher slug (nrwl.angular-console) and the four IOC SHA256s; extension-folder drops are nearly exclusively triggered by the VS Code installer and the named publisher. Cross-checked against: • https://nx.dev/blog/nx-console-incident • https://www.ox.security/blog/nx-console-supply-chain-attack • https://stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-supply-chain-attack-iocs

[LLM] VS Code Code.exe spawns shell running 'MCP setup' style curl/wget from nrwl/nx GitHub raw Installation High
Hunts the trojan's startup behaviour: the malicious Nx Console extension silently shelled out to a one-liner disguised as MCP setup that downloaded a hidden payload from a planted commit on the official nrwl/nx GitHub repo. Pivots on Code.exe → shell → curl/wget reaching raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx. Rationale: Targets the precise OX Security finding: Code.exe → shell → fetch hidden payload from nrwl/nx GitHub, masquerading as MCP setup. Joining the parent (VS Code), child (interpreter), and payload string (nrwl/nx or MCP) makes the AND triple highly specific. Cross-checked against: • https://www.ox.security/blog/nx-console-supply-chain-attack • https://nx.dev/blog/nx-console-incident
ATT&CKT1059.003 T1059.004 T1105 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("Code.exe", "Code - Insiders.exe", "Cursor.exe", "code-tunnel.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "bash.exe", "sh.exe", "wsl.exe", "node.exe", "npx.cmd", "npm.cmd")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("nrwl/nx", "raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl", "github.com/nrwl/nx")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl", "wget", "Invoke-WebRequest", "iwr", "Start-BitsTransfer") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("MCP", "mcp-setup", "mcpServers"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp asc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("Code.exe", "Code - Insiders.exe", "Cursor.exe", "code-tunnel.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "bash.exe", "sh.exe", "wsl.exe", "node.exe", "npx.cmd", "npm.cmd")
| where CommandLine has_any ("nrwl/nx", "raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl", "github.com/nrwl/nx")
   or (CommandLine has_any ("curl", "wget", "Invoke-WebRequest", "iwr", "Start-BitsTransfer") and CommandLine has_any ("MCP", "mcp-setup", "mcpServers"))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated asc

detection:

      - '\Code - Insiders.exe'
      - '\Cursor.exe'

  child:

source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\Code.exe OR *\\Code\ -\ Insiders.exe OR *\\Cursor.exe OR *\\code-tunnel.exe) @Image:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\bash.exe OR *\\sh.exe OR *\\wsl.exe OR *\\node.exe) @CommandLine:(*nrwl/nx* OR *raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl* OR *github.com/nrwl/nx*)

[LLM] VS Code child shell accessing 1Password / Claude Code / npm / AWS / GitHub crede Actions on Objectives High
Hunts the credential-harvest payload behaviour: a shell spawned by Code.exe touching 1Password vault files, ~/.claude config, .npmrc, .aws/credentials, and GitHub PAT / SSH key stores. The article calls out these five targets explicitly as the stealer's scope. Rationale: Joins the article-named parent (VS Code / Cursor where Nx Console installs) with shell children plus the five named credential targets (1Password, Anthropic Claude Code, npm, GitHub, AWS). The combination of all three layers is what makes it specific to this campaign rather than benign dev work. Cross-checked against: • https://www.ox.security/blog/nx-console-supply-chain-attack • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/team-pcp-nx-console-credential-stealer • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/
ATT&CKT1555 T1552.001 T1552.004 T1083

[LLM] Egress to TeamPCP credential-stealer infrastructure (94.154.172.43 / 45.148.10.212 / lookalike domains) Command & Control High
Hunts outbound connections / DNS to the TeamPCP infrastructure shared across the Nx Console, TanStack, Mistral, Grafana, and durabletask campaigns. The lookalike domains (checkmarx.cx, scan.aquasecurtiy.org, git-tanstack.com) and dedicated drops audit.checkmarx.cx, api.masscan.cloud, checkmarx.zone are all specific to this actor's exfil routing. Rationale: All five domains and both IPs are corroborated across StepSecurity, Wiz, JFrog, and Socket.dev reports for TeamPCP. The lookalike domains (checkmarx.cx vs checkmarx.com, aquasecurtiy vs aquasecurity) are uniquely typosquatted IOCs and produce near-zero benign hits. Cross-checked against: • https://stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-supply-chain-attack-iocs • https://socket.dev/blog/shai-hulud-nx-console • https://www.wiz.io/blog/teampcp-durabletask-pypi • https://jfrog.com/blog/shai-hulud-iocs
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568.002 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
let BadIPs = dynamic(["94.154.172.43", "45.148.10.212"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["audit.checkmarx.cx", "checkmarx.zone", "scan.aquasecurtiy.org", "git-tanstack.com", "api.masscan.cloud"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (BadIPs) or RemoteUrl has_any (BadDomains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp asc
let BadIPs = dynamic(["94.154.172.43", "45.148.10.212"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["audit.checkmarx.cx", "checkmarx.zone", "scan.aquasecurtiy.org", "git-tanstack.com", "api.masscan.cloud"]);
union isfuzzy=true
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where DestinationIP in (BadIPs) or RequestURL has_any (BadDomains) or DestinationHostName has_any (BadDomains)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="CommonSecurityLog", Host=SourceHostName, User=SourceUserName, DestIP=DestinationIP, DestHost=coalesce(DestinationHostName, RequestURL), App=ApplicationProtocol),
    (DnsEvents
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where Name has_any (BadDomains)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="DnsEvents", Host=Computer, User="", DestIP=tostring(ClientIP), DestHost=Name, App="dns"),
    (ImNetworkSession
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs) or DstHostname has_any (BadDomains)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="ImNetworkSession", Host=SrcHostname, User=SrcUsername, DestIP=DstIpAddr, DestHost=DstHostname, App=NetworkApplicationProtocol)
| order by TimeGenerated asc

[LLM] Bulk GitHub repository clone fan-out from a single account (TeamPCP 3,800-repo exfil pattern) Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the actions phase of the campaign: GitHub itself reported ~3,800 internal repos cloned after TeamPCP harvested a developer's PAT/SSH key. Detects an unusual surge of git clone operations or GitHub API repo downloads from a single user/IP within a tight window. Rationale: Targets GitHub's reported impact statement: a single dev's stolen token was used to pull ~3,800 internal repos. The 50-clone-per-hour threshold is well above typical developer behaviour (a busy day for a single dev tops out around 10-15 unique clones). Cross-checked against: • https://github.blog/security/incident-response-may-2026 • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1213/003/
ATT&CKT1213.003 T1530 T1567
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Web.Web
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("git.exe", "gh.exe", "curl.exe", "wget.exe", "node.exe", "pwsh.exe", "powershell.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("git clone", "gh repo clone", "api.github.com/repos", ".git")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("github.com/", "api.github.com", "raw.githubusercontent.com")
| summarize CloneCount = count(), Repos = make_set(extract(@"github\.com[:/]([\w\-\.]+/[\w\-\.]+?)(?:\.git|\s|$)", 1, ProcessCommandLine), 200), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, AccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where CloneCount > 50
| order by CloneCount desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any ("git.exe", "gh.exe", "curl.exe", "wget.exe", "node.exe", "pwsh.exe", "powershell.exe")
| where CommandLine has_any ("git clone", "gh repo clone", "api.github.com/repos", ".git")
| where CommandLine has_any ("github.com/", "api.github.com", "raw.githubusercontent.com")
| summarize CloneCount = count(), Repos = make_set(extract(@"github\.com[:/]([\w\-\.]+/[\w\-\.]+?)(?:\.git|\s|$)", 1, CommandLine), 200), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by Computer, Account, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where CloneCount > 50
| order by CloneCount desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\git.exe OR *\\gh.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\wget.exe OR *\\node.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\powershell.exe) @CommandLine:((*"git clone"* OR *"gh repo clone"* OR *api.github.com/repos* OR *.git*) AND (*github.com/* OR *api.github.com* OR *raw.githubusercontent.com*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/(git|gh|curl|wget|node|pwsh|powershell)\.exe$/i
| regex("(git clone|gh repo clone|api\\.github\\.com/repos|\\.git)", field=CommandLine)
| regex("(github\\.com|api\\.github\\.com|raw\\.githubusercontent\\.com)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, bucket(field=_time, span=1h)], function=count(as=CloneCount))
| CloneCount > 50
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("git.exe","git","gh.exe","gh","curl.exe","curl","wget.exe","wget") (Processes.process="*git clone*" OR Processes.process="*api.github.com/repos*" OR Processes.process="*gh repo clone*" OR Processes.process="*github.com/*.git*") by Processes.dest Processes.user span=1h | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where count > 50 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("git.exe","git","gh.exe","gh","curl.exe","curl","wget.exe","wget") (Processes.process="*git clone*" OR Processes.process="*api.github.com/repos*" OR Processes.process="*gh repo clone*" OR Processes.process="*github.com/*.git*") by Processes.dest Processes.user span=1h | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where count > 50 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c", "acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf", "9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99") or SHA1 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c", "acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf", "9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99") or MD5 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c", "acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf", "9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c", "acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf", "9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99") or SHA1 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c", "acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf", "9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99") or MD5 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c", "acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf", "9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c", "acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf", "9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

CISA KEV: CVE-2025-34291 — Langflow Origin Validation Error Vulnerability

CISA KEV
2026-05-21 1 use case 0 techniques 3 kill-chain phases detected

Langflow contains an origin validation error vulnerability in which an overly permissive CORS configuration combined with a refresh token cookie configured as SameSite=None allows a malicious webpage to perform cross-origin requests that include credentials and successfully call the refresh endpoint. This could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary code and achieve full system compromise via obtained tokens that permit access to authenticated endpoints. Vendor: Langflow, Product: Langflow. Federal patch due: 2026-06-04.
