Mini Shai Hulud: Compromised @antv npm packages enable CI/CD credential theft

Microsoft Security BlogStepSecurity
2026-05-20 13 use cases 2 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Three malicious versions of Microsoft's official durabletask Python SDK were published to PyPI on May 19, 2026. The compromised package silently downloads and executes a 28 KB payload that steals credentials from AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, password managers, and over 90 developer tool configurations, then spreads laterally through cloud infrastructure. The payload skips systems with a Russian locale, a hallmark of Eastern European cybercrime operations. The attack has been linked to the TeamPCP threat group behind the Mini Shai-Hulud campaign.

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud durabletask dropper C2 callback to git-service.com Command & Control High
Detects outbound connections to the TeamPCP-controlled domains check.git-service.com / git-service.com / t.m-kosche.com or the hosting IP 160.119.64.3, particularly when initiated by a python3 process — the durabletask malicious __init__.py uses urllib.request.urlretrieve against check.git-service.com to fetch rope.pyz. Rationale: Domains check.git-service.com, git-service.com, t.m-kosche.com and IP 160.119.64.3 are explicit campaign IOCs in the Microsoft post. The article ties t.m-kosche[.]com to TeamPCP's broader Mini Shai-Hulud campaign that also hit TanStack, Mistral AI, LiteLLM and @antv — so these are high-fidelity even outside the durabletask scope.

[LLM] durabletask second-stage dropper: python3 executing /tmp/managed.pyz Installation High
Detects execution of /tmp/managed.pyz by python3 — the rope.pyz cloud-intrusion framework dropped to /tmp/managed.pyz by the compromised durabletask __init__.py. The dropper spawns four parallel child instances within ~4 seconds. Rationale: The article gives the exact dropper code (`subprocess.Popen(["python3","/tmp/managed.pyz"], ...)`) and the Harden-Runner process tree confirms /tmp/managed.pyz as the canonical second-stage path. This string is unique to TeamPCP's tooling.

[LLM] gh CLI token enumeration via python parent (managed.pyz credential exfil) Actions on Objectives High
Detects `gh auth token` and `gh auth status --show-token` invocations whose parent is python3 or whose grandparent is /tmp/managed.pyz — the credential-access path used by all four parallel rope.pyz collector instances to harvest GitHub tokens. Rationale: The Harden-Runner process tree in the article shows each of the 4 managed.pyz children running `gh auth token` and `gh auth status --show-token` back-to-back. Pairing those exact subcommands with a python parent makes the detection nearly FP-free outside of legitimate Python-based GH automation.

[LLM] Fake pgsql-monitor.service systemd user persistence Installation High
Detects creation of a systemd user unit named pgsql-monitor.service or invocation of `systemctl --user daemon-reload` by a python process — the persistence mechanism rope.pyz installs to survive runner restarts. The fake unit masquerades as a Postgres monitoring service. Rationale: The article explicitly names `pgsql-monitor.service` as the persistence artifact and shows `systemctl --user daemon-reload` in every one of the 4 managed.pyz child processes. The service name is highly specific to this campaign — legitimate PostgreSQL monitoring uses entirely different unit names (postgresql-exporter, prometheus-postgres-exporter, pg_stat_monitor, etc.).

[LLM] Single python parent fans out 3+ managed.pyz children within seconds Installation High
Detects the rope.pyz signature behaviour: one `python3 -c "import durabletask"` parent that spawns 3+ child `python3 /tmp/managed.pyz` processes within a 60s window. The article documents 4 parallel collector instances completing credential theft in under 4 seconds — this temporal/fan-out shape is rare outside the campaign. Rationale: The Harden-Runner process tree in the article documents exactly 4 managed.pyz children (PIDs 2380, 2404, 2430, 2432) under a single `python3 -c "import durabletask"` parent, with the entire chain completing in <4 seconds. Threshold of ≥3 children within 60s is well below the observed fan-out — legitimate multiprocessing apps don't use this path/name.
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1106
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/managed.pyz"
| summarize ChildCount = count(),
            FirstChild = min(Timestamp),
            LastChild = max(Timestamp),
            ChildPIDs = make_set(ProcessId, 10),
            SampleCmd = any(ProcessCommandLine)
            by DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, AccountName
| extend SpawnWindowSec = datetime_diff('second', LastChild, FirstChild)
| where ChildCount >= 3 and SpawnWindowSec <= 60
| order by FirstChild desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/managed.pyz"
| summarize ChildCount = count(),
            FirstChild = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastChild = max(TimeGenerated),
            SampleCmd = any(TargetProcessCommandLine)
            by DvcHostname, ActingProcessId, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| extend SpawnWindowSec = datetime_diff('second', LastChild, FirstChild)
| where ChildCount >= 3 and SpawnWindowSec <= 60
| order by FirstChild desc
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.command_line:*/tmp/managed.pyz*
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 CommandLine=/\/tmp\/managed\.pyz/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, UserName], function={ ChildCount := count() | FirstSeen := min(@timestamp) | LastSeen := max(@timestamp) })
| ChildCount >= 3
| SpawnWindowSec := (LastSeen - FirstSeen) / 1000
| SpawnWindowSec <= 60
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process_id) as child_pids from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process="*/tmp/managed.pyz*" by Processes.dest Processes.parent_process_id Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| where count >= 3
| eval spawn_window_sec = lastTime - firstTime
| where spawn_window_sec <= 60
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process_id) as child_pids from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process="*/tmp/managed.pyz*" by Processes.dest Processes.parent_process_id Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.user

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142") or SHA1 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142") or MD5 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142") or SHA1 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142") or MD5 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud C2 callback to zero.masscan.cloud / 94.154.172.43 Command & Control High
Detects network or DNS activity reaching the @cap-js compromise C2 endpoints (zero.masscan.cloud, 94.154.172.43). Any host resolving or connecting to these indicators after April 29, 2026 is highly suspicious because the domain belongs to TeamPCP's Shai-Hulud exfiltration infrastructure. Rationale: zero.masscan.cloud and 94.154.172.43 are the C2 endpoints called out in the GHSA-pvw4-cvr4-97p8 advisory and corroborated by Socket.dev, JFrog, and StepSecurity research into the Mini Shai-Hulud campaign. Any resolution or connection to these IOCs after April 29, 2026 is a high-fidelity post-compromise signal. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pvw4-cvr4-97p8 • https://socket.dev/blog/shai-hulud-2-0 • https://jfrog.com/blog/shai-hulud-npm-supply-chain • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/shai-hulud-antv-compromise
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
let MaliciousDomains = dynamic(["zero.masscan.cloud"]);
let MaliciousIPs = dynamic(["94.154.172.43"]);
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where RemoteIP in (MaliciousIPs) or RemoteUrl has_any (MaliciousDomains)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
            InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
            InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
            InitiatingProcessParentFileName;
let DnsHits = DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ActionType in ("DnsQueryResponse","DnsConnectionInspected","InboundConnectionAccepted")
  | where RemoteUrl has_any (MaliciousDomains) or RemoteIP in (MaliciousIPs)
     or AdditionalFields has "masscan.cloud" or AdditionalFields has "94.154.172.43"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl,
            InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, AdditionalFields;
union NetHits, DnsHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let MaliciousDomains = dynamic(["zero.masscan.cloud"]);
let MaliciousIPs = dynamic(["94.154.172.43"]);
let Dns = ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any (MaliciousDomains) or DnsResponseName has_any (MaliciousIPs)
  | project TimeGenerated, Source="ImDnsActivity", Host=DvcHostname, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr,
            Query=DnsQuery, Response=DnsResponseName, User=SrcUsername;
let NetSess = ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DstIpAddr in (MaliciousIPs) or DstHostname has_any (MaliciousDomains) or Url has_any (MaliciousDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, Source="ImNetworkSession", Host=DvcHostname, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr,
            Query=DstHostname, Response=DstIpAddr, User=SrcUsername;
let Cef = CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DestinationIP in (MaliciousIPs) or DestinationHostName has_any (MaliciousDomains)
     or RequestURL has_any (MaliciousDomains) or DestinationDnsDomain has_any (MaliciousDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, Source="CommonSecurityLog", Host=SourceHostName, SrcIp=SourceIP,
            Query=coalesce(DestinationHostName, DestinationDnsDomain, RequestURL),
            Response=DestinationIP, User=SourceUserName;
union Dns, NetSess, Cef
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Mini Shai-Hulud (@cap-js) C2 callback to zero.masscan.cloud or 94.154.172.43
id: 8b3c1f4e-2d6a-4f97-b011-a4b8e22f1d77
description: Detects network or DNS resolution to the Mini Shai-Hulud (TeamPCP) C2 endpoints associated with CVE-2026-46421 supply chain compromise of @cap-js/sqlite, @cap-js/postgres and @cap-js/db-service.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pvw4-cvr4-97p8
  - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-46421
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.exfiltration
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1071.004
  - attack.t1041
logsource:
  category: dns
detection:
  selection_domain:
    query|contains:
      - 'zero.masscan.cloud'
      - 'masscan.cloud'
  selection_ip:
    answer:
      - '94.154.172.43'
  condition: selection_domain or selection_ip
level: high
(source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd OR linux.syslog OR azure.activity_logs OR cloudtrail) AND (@DestinationHostname:(*zero.masscan.cloud* OR *masscan.cloud*) OR @DestinationIp:94.154.172.43 OR @network.destination.ip:94.154.172.43 OR @dns.question.name:(*zero.masscan.cloud* OR *masscan.cloud*) OR @network.client.ip:94.154.172.43))
(#event_simpleName=DnsRequest OR #event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 OR #event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP6)
| (DomainName=/(^|\.)masscan\.cloud$/i OR DomainName=/^zero\.masscan\.cloud$/i OR RemoteAddressIP4="94.154.172.43" OR RemoteAddressIP6="94.154.172.43" OR FirstIP4Record="94.154.172.43")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName, RemoteAddressIP4], function=count())

[LLM] Compromised @cap-js stealer artefact hash present on disk or in execution Installation High
Detects on-disk or in-execution presence of the three known SHA256 artefacts shipped inside the trojanised @cap-js/sqlite 2.2.2, @cap-js/postgres 2.2.2, and @cap-js/db-service 2.10.1 packages. A hash hit is deterministic evidence of installation of the compromised version and triggers credential-rotation playbooks. Rationale: The three SHA256 hashes are the artefacts called out directly in GHSA-pvw4-cvr4-97p8 for CVE-2026-46421 and corroborated by Socket.dev and JFrog IOC bundles for the @cap-js Mini Shai-Hulud campaign. A hash hit is deterministic and not subject to false positives outside controlled malware-analysis hosts. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pvw4-cvr4-97p8 • https://socket.dev/blog/shai-hulud-2-0 • https://jfrog.com/blog/shai-hulud-npm-supply-chain
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1552.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes

  "4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34",
  "6f933d00b7d05678eb43c90963a80b8947c4ae6830182f89df31da9f568fea95",
  "eb6eb4154b03ec73218727dc643d26f4e14dfda2438112926bb5daf37ae8bcdb"]);
let FileHits = DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(90d)
  | where SHA256 in (CapJsHashes)
  | project Timestamp, Source="DeviceFileEvents", DeviceId, DeviceName,
            FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
            InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
            InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath;
let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(90d)
  | where SHA256 in (CapJsHashes) or InitiatingProcessSHA256 in (CapJsHashes)
  | project Timestamp, Source="DeviceProcessEvents", DeviceId, DeviceName,
            FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
            InitiatingProcessFileName=InitiatingProcessFileName,
            InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName,
            InitiatingProcessFolderPath=InitiatingProcessFolderPath;
let ImgHits = DeviceImageLoadEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(90d)
  | where SHA256 in (CapJsHashes)
  | project Timestamp, Source="DeviceImageLoadEvents", DeviceId, DeviceName,
            FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
            InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
            InitiatingProcessAccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName,

union FileHits, ProcHits, ImgHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let CapJsHashes = dynamic([

  "6f933d00b7d05678eb43c90963a80b8947c4ae6830182f89df31da9f568fea95",
  "eb6eb4154b03ec73218727dc643d26f4e14dfda2438112926bb5daf37ae8bcdb"]);

            User=ActorUsername, Process=ActingProcessName, Cmd=ActingProcessCommandLine,

let ProcHits = ImProcessCreate

  | where SHA256 in (CapJsHashes) or Hash in (CapJsHashes)
  | project TimeGenerated, Source="ImProcessCreate", Host=DvcHostname,
            User=ActorUsername, Process=TargetProcessName, Cmd=TargetProcessCommandLine,
            FilePath=TargetProcessName, FileName=TargetProcessName,
            HashValue=coalesce(SHA256, Hash);
let CefHits = CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
  | where FileHash in (CapJsHashes)
  | project TimeGenerated, Source="CommonSecurityLog", Host=SourceHostName,
            User=SourceUserName, Process=SourceProcessName, Cmd=DeviceCustomString1,
            FilePath=FilePath, FileName=FileName, HashValue=FileHash;
union FileHits, ProcHits, CefHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-46421")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-46421")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-46421")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-46421")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "6f933d00b7d05678eb43c90963a80b8947c4ae6830182f89df31da9f568fea95", "eb6eb4154b03ec73218727dc643d26f4e14dfda2438112926bb5daf37ae8bcdb") or SHA1 in~ ("4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "6f933d00b7d05678eb43c90963a80b8947c4ae6830182f89df31da9f568fea95", "eb6eb4154b03ec73218727dc643d26f4e14dfda2438112926bb5daf37ae8bcdb") or MD5 in~ ("4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "6f933d00b7d05678eb43c90963a80b8947c4ae6830182f89df31da9f568fea95", "eb6eb4154b03ec73218727dc643d26f4e14dfda2438112926bb5daf37ae8bcdb")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "6f933d00b7d05678eb43c90963a80b8947c4ae6830182f89df31da9f568fea95", "eb6eb4154b03ec73218727dc643d26f4e14dfda2438112926bb5daf37ae8bcdb") or SHA1 in~ ("4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "6f933d00b7d05678eb43c90963a80b8947c4ae6830182f89df31da9f568fea95", "eb6eb4154b03ec73218727dc643d26f4e14dfda2438112926bb5daf37ae8bcdb") or MD5 in~ ("4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "6f933d00b7d05678eb43c90963a80b8947c4ae6830182f89df31da9f568fea95", "eb6eb4154b03ec73218727dc643d26f4e14dfda2438112926bb5daf37ae8bcdb")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "6f933d00b7d05678eb43c90963a80b8947c4ae6830182f89df31da9f568fea95", "eb6eb4154b03ec73218727dc643d26f4e14dfda2438112926bb5daf37ae8bcdb"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] VS Code/Cursor extension host fetches dropper from nrwl/nx orphan commit on GitHub · [LLM] macOS Python backdoor persistence via kitty-monitor LaunchAgent and cat.py drop · [LLM] Python backdoor self-daemonisation via __DAEMONIZED=1 spawned by VS Code helper or node · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] VS Code extension host fan-out reads of developer secrets (.ssh, .aws, .npmrc, ~/.claude/settings.json) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
[LLM] Nx Console v18.95.0 compromised extension installed (May 2026 supply-chain attack) Delivery High
Detects installation of the poisoned Nx Console (nrwl.angular-console) v18.95.0 VS Code extension that was published with stolen credentials on 2026-05-18 and pulled by 2.2M+ install base via auto-update. Matches on the known SHA256/SHA1 of the malicious build and the version-pinned extension folder path written by Code.exe / Cursor.exe / node.exe extension hosts. Rationale: Anchors directly on the article-named extension identifier (nrwl.angular-console) and version 18.95.0, plus the four SHA256/SHA1 hashes of the malicious build supplied by the Nx maintainers' advisory. Hashes plus version-pinned path give near-zero FP and cover both fresh installs and offline re-imaging. Cross-checked against GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w and StepSecurity's IOC writeup. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://cybersecuritynews.com/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised/

[LLM] VS Code/Cursor extension host fetches dropper from nrwl/nx orphan commit on GitHub Installation Medium
The compromised Nx Console v18.95.0 pulled a 498 KB obfuscated dropper hidden in an orphan (dangling) commit on the legitimate nrwl/nx GitHub repository. This UC hunts VS Code / Cursor / their Node extension-host processes contacting raw.githubusercontent.com or codeload.github.com on nrwl/nx paths — a request shape that the legitimate Nx Console does not make at runtime. Rationale: Anchors on the article's explicit claim that the 498 KB dropper was hidden in an orphan commit of the legitimate nrwl/nx GitHub repository — a request the unmodified Nx Console extension does not make. Pairs the VS Code / Cursor / extension-host process identity with the unique nrwl/nx GitHub raw/codeload/blob API paths. Cross-checked against GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w and StepSecurity which confirm the orphan-commit dropper mechanism. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html
ATT&CKT1105 T1102.001
Data sourcesWeb Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("code.exe","cursor.exe","node.exe","code-insiders.exe","codium.exe","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)","cursor-helper")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("code.exe","cursor.exe","code-insiders.exe")
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx/","codeload.github.com/nrwl/nx/","api.github.com/repos/nrwl/nx/git/blobs","api.github.com/repos/nrwl/nx/git/trees")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Url has_any ("raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx/","codeload.github.com/nrwl/nx/","api.github.com/repos/nrwl/nx/git/blobs","api.github.com/repos/nrwl/nx/git/trees")
   or HttpHostName in~ ("raw.githubusercontent.com","codeload.github.com") and UrlOriginal has "nrwl/nx"
| where SrcUsername != "" and (HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent has_any ("VSCode","vscode","Cursor","node-fetch","axios","got","undici") or DvcHostname != "")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, Url, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, HttpResponseBodyBytes
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] macOS Python backdoor persistence via kitty-monitor LaunchAgent and cat.py drop Installation High
After execution, the poisoned Nx Console payload drops a Python backdoor on macOS at ~/.local/share/kitty/cat.py and registers a LaunchAgent at ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.user.kitty-monitor.plist plus the state file /var/tmp/.gh_update_state. The backdoor uses the GitHub Search API as a dead-drop resolver for follow-on commands. This UC alerts on file creation of any of these named artifacts. Rationale: Anchors on three specific filesystem artifacts disclosed in the GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w and corroborated by StepSecurity / The Hacker News: the kitty-monitor LaunchAgent (T1543.001 macOS persistence), the cat.py Python dropper under ~/.local/share/kitty/, and the /var/tmp/.gh_update_state semaphore. None of these names belong to any legitimate kitty terminal install (which doesn't write LaunchAgents under com.user.*). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html
ATT&CKT1543.001 T1102.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FolderPath endswith "/.local/share/kitty/cat.py")
   or (FolderPath endswith "/Library/LaunchAgents/com.user.kitty-monitor.plist")
   or (FolderPath == "/var/tmp/.gh_update_state")
   or (FolderPath startswith "/tmp/kitty-")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where (TargetFilePath endswith "/.local/share/kitty/cat.py")
   or (TargetFilePath endswith "/Library/LaunchAgents/com.user.kitty-monitor.plist")
   or (TargetFilePath == "/var/tmp/.gh_update_state")
   or (TargetFilePath startswith "/tmp/kitty-")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Python backdoor self-daemonisation via __DAEMONIZED=1 spawned by VS Code helper or node Installation Medium
The Nx Console v18.95.0 macOS backdoor re-execs itself with __DAEMONIZED=1 in its environment to detach from the VS Code extension host parent — a distinctive marker used by cat.py. This UC hunts python processes spawned by code/cursor/node/shell parents that either run cat.py from the kitty directory or carry the __DAEMONIZED=1 token in their command-line / parent command-line. Rationale: The __DAEMONIZED=1 environment-variable self-relaunch is a distinctive marker called out by the GitHub Security Advisory and StepSecurity writeup for the cat.py backdoor — legitimate Python tooling does not use this sentinel. Combining it with the kitty/cat.py path and a VS Code helper / node / shell parent yields high fidelity. Cross-checked against GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w and StepSecurity IOC list. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1564.012 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("python","python3","python3.9","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12","python.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("cat.py","/.local/share/kitty/","/tmp/kitty-","__DAEMONIZED=1")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("__DAEMONIZED=1","cat.py","/.local/share/kitty/")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)","Code","Cursor","cursor-helper","sh","zsh","bash","python","python3")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, ProcessId, InitiatingProcessId
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|/)python(3(\.[0-9]+)?)?(\.exe)?$"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("cat.py","/.local/share/kitty/","/tmp/kitty-","__DAEMONIZED=1")
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("__DAEMONIZED=1","cat.py")
| where ParentProcessName in~ ("node","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)","Code","Cursor","cursor-helper","sh","zsh","bash","python","python3")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Nx Console Compromise - Python cat.py Daemon Spawned by Code Helper or Node
id: 9e2b5a14-7c83-4d09-b6e5-2a8f1c4d5e6f
description: Detects the Python backdoor cat.py (or its __DAEMONIZED=1 self-relaunch) launched by a VS Code helper, Cursor helper, node or shell parent. Specific to the May 2026 Nx Console v18.95.0 supply-chain compromise.
references:
    - https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w
    - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
    - attack.t1059.006
    - attack.execution
    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: macos
detection:
    selection_python:
        Image|endswith:
            - '/python'
            - '/python3'
            - '/python3.9'
            - '/python3.10'
            - '/python3.11'
            - '/python3.12'
    selection_payload:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'cat.py'
            - '/.local/share/kitty/'
            - '/tmp/kitty-'
            - '__DAEMONIZED=1'
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '/Code Helper'
            - '/Code Helper (Plugin)'
            - '/Code Helper (Renderer)'
            - '/cursor-helper'
            - '/Cursor'
            - '/node'
            - '/sh'
            - '/zsh'
            - '/bash'
            - '/python'
            - '/python3'
    condition: selection_python and selection_payload and selection_parent
falsepositives:
    - Researcher reproducing the IOC in a sandbox with an annotated commandline
level: high

source:(linux.auditd OR windows.sysmon) (@process.name:(python OR python3 OR python3.9 OR python3.10 OR python3.11 OR python3.12) OR @Image:(*/python OR */python3 OR *\\python.exe)) (@process.command_line:(*cat.py* OR */.local/share/kitty/* OR */tmp/kitty-* OR *__DAEMONIZED=1*) OR @CommandLine:(*cat.py* OR *__DAEMONIZED=1*)) (@process.parent.name:(node OR Code\ Helper OR cursor-helper OR Cursor OR sh OR zsh OR bash OR python OR python3) OR @ParentImage:(*\\node.exe OR *Code\ Helper* OR *cursor-helper*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/python(3(\.[0-9]+)?)?$/i
| (CommandLine=/cat\.py/i OR CommandLine=/\/\.local\/share\/kitty\//i OR CommandLine=/\/tmp\/kitty-/i OR CommandLine=/__DAEMONIZED=1/i)
| ParentBaseFileName=/(Code Helper|cursor-helper|Cursor|node|bash|zsh|sh|python3?)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("python","python3","python3.9","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12") AND (Processes.process IN ("*cat.py*","*/.local/share/kitty/*","*/tmp/kitty-*","*__DAEMONIZED=1*") OR Processes.parent_process IN ("*__DAEMONIZED=1*","*cat.py*")) AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("node","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)","Code","Cursor","cursor-helper","sh","zsh","bash","python","python3") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("python","python3","python3.9","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12") AND (Processes.process IN ("*cat.py*","*/.local/share/kitty/*","*/tmp/kitty-*","*__DAEMONIZED=1*") OR Processes.parent_process IN ("*__DAEMONIZED=1*","*cat.py*")) AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("node","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)","Code","Cursor","cursor-helper","sh","zsh","bash","python","python3") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] VS Code extension host fan-out reads of developer secrets (.ssh, .aws, .npmrc, ~/.claude/settings.json) Actions on Objectives Medium
The poisoned Nx Console payload sweeps developer credentials from a fixed list — SSH private keys, AWS credentials, npm tokens, Claude Code config (~/.claude/settings.json — believed to be the first supply-chain payload to target an AI assistant config), gcloud, kube, gnupg, docker, and .env files. This UC alerts when the VS Code / Cursor extension-host Node process touches ≥4 distinct credential-bearing paths within a 10-minute window — a shape no legitimate extension exhibits. Rationale: Anchors on the exact credential-file list disclosed by the GitHub Security Advisory and StepSecurity for the cat.py / Nx Console payload, including the novel target ~/.claude/settings.json that the article calls out as one of the first AI-assistant config harvest behaviours seen in the wild. The ≥4-distinct-paths threshold within 10 minutes is a sweep marker that no legitimate VS Code extension exhibits. Cross-checked GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w + StepSecurity + The Hacker News. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html • https://cybersecuritynews.com/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileAccessed","FileRead","FileOpened")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)","cursor-helper","Cursor","Code","code.exe","cursor.exe","python","python3")
| where (FolderPath has_any ("/.ssh/","/.aws/","/.config/gcloud/","/.kube/","/.docker/","/.gnupg/","/.claude/")
     or FileName in~ ("id_rsa","id_ed25519","id_ecdsa","credentials","known_hosts","authorized_keys",".npmrc","settings.json","config.json")
     or FileName =~ ".env" or FileName startswith ".env." or FolderPath has "/.npmrc")
| where not (FolderPath has "/.claude/" and FileName != "settings.json")    // narrow .claude noise — only the settings.json file matters
| summarize PathCount = dcount(strcat(FolderPath, FileName)),
            Paths = make_set(strcat(FolderPath, FileName), 25),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
            by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, bin(Timestamp, 10m)
| where PathCount >= 4    // 4 = sweep threshold; one-off .env read is normal dev work, ≥4 distinct cred files in 10 min is harvesting behaviour
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("node","node.exe","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)","cursor-helper","Cursor","Code","code.exe","cursor.exe","python","python3")
| where (TargetFilePath has_any ("/.ssh/","/.aws/","/.config/gcloud/","/.kube/","/.docker/","/.gnupg/","/.claude/")
     or TargetFileName in~ ("id_rsa","id_ed25519","id_ecdsa","credentials","known_hosts","authorized_keys",".npmrc")
     or TargetFileName =~ ".env" or TargetFileName startswith ".env."
     or (TargetFilePath has "/.claude/" and TargetFileName =~ "settings.json"))
| summarize PathCount = dcount(TargetFilePath),
            Paths = make_set(TargetFilePath, 25),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
| where PathCount >= 4    // 4 = empirical sweep threshold
| order by FirstSeen desc
source:(linux.auditd OR windows.sysmon) (@process.name:(node OR python OR python3) OR @Image:(*\\node.exe OR *Code\ Helper* OR *cursor-helper* OR *\\Code.exe OR *\\Cursor.exe)) (@file.path:(*/.ssh/id_rsa OR */.ssh/id_ed25519 OR */.ssh/id_ecdsa OR */.aws/credentials OR */.aws/config OR */.npmrc OR */.config/gcloud/* OR */.kube/config OR */.docker/config.json OR */.gnupg/* OR */.claude/settings.json OR */.env OR */.env.*) OR @TargetFilename:(*\\.ssh\\id_rsa OR *\\.aws\\credentials OR *\\.npmrc OR *\\.claude\\settings.json OR *\\.env))
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo ContextImageFileName=/(node|Code Helper|cursor-helper|Cursor|Code|python3?)\.?(exe)?$/i
| (TargetFileName=/\/\.ssh\/(id_(rsa|ed25519|ecdsa)|known_hosts|config|authorized_keys)$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.aws\/(credentials|config)$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.npmrc$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.config\/gcloud\//i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.kube\/config$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.docker\/config\.json$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.gnupg\//i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.claude\/settings\.json$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.env(\.[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)?$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, bucket(span=10m)], function=[count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true, as=PathCount), collect(TargetFileName, multival=true)])
| PathCount >= 4
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count dc(Filesystem.file_path) as distinct_paths values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path IN ("*/.ssh/id_rsa","*/.ssh/id_ed25519","*/.ssh/id_ecdsa","*/.ssh/known_hosts","*/.ssh/config","*/.aws/credentials","*/.aws/config","*/.npmrc","*/.config/gcloud/*","*/.kube/config","*/.docker/config.json","*/.gnupg/*","*/.claude/settings.json","*/.env","*/.env.*")) AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("node","node.exe","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)","cursor-helper","Cursor","Code","python","python3") by host Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name span=10m | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where distinct_paths >= 4 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count dc(Filesystem.file_path) as distinct_paths values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path IN ("*/.ssh/id_rsa","*/.ssh/id_ed25519","*/.ssh/id_ecdsa","*/.ssh/known_hosts","*/.ssh/config","*/.aws/credentials","*/.aws/config","*/.npmrc","*/.config/gcloud/*","*/.kube/config","*/.docker/config.json","*/.gnupg/*","*/.claude/settings.json","*/.env","*/.env.*")) AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("node","node.exe","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)","cursor-helper","Cursor","Code","python","python3") by host Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name span=10m | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where distinct_paths >= 4 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48027")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48027")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT

| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
